title: Fractional reservation orchestrator and surge spillover throttle
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation:
This change introduces a fractional reservation orchestration layer and a surge spillover throttle that together allow Dedicated fleets to support sub-unit (fractional) reservation commitments, progressively honor short-term surge requests, and bound cross-tenant spillover during capacity exhaustion. Customers asked for smoother degradation when their committed units are partially saturated while still allowing opportunistic bursts without violating throughput guarantees for committed tenants.

What it does (high level):
- FractionalReservationOrchestrator: tracks per-tenant committed units at sub-integer granularity (e.g. 0.25 slots). It maintains a lightweight ledger that aggregates fractional credits and periodically consolidates them into the standard reservation pool for admission decisions.
- SurgeSpilloverThrottle: when pool-level capacity is constrained, the throttle enforces a probabilistic soft-fence that routes excess requests into spill lanes with capped acceptance probability and optional latency hedging. Spill lanes are recorded separately in utilization fingerprints so accounting does not accidentally reduce committed tenant guarantees.
- Local warmset accounting and reconciliation hooks ensure that short-lived warmlet pre-warms are considered when computing effective headroom.

Design notes and tradeoffs:
- Fractional reservations reduce churn when customers scale by small increments; consolidation is batched to avoid frequent global coordination. We accept short windows of inaccuracy (seconds) in favor of lower control-plane overhead.
- The spillover throttle uses a tunable acceptance curve (exponential backoff by utilization percentile) to favor small bursts. This intentionally compromises 100% throughput for non-committed traffic to protect SLOs.
- Telemetry: new counters and HDR sketches provide percentile-based acceptance and spill rates per-tenant and per-pool.

API and config changes:
- New config block under dedicated.autoscaler.fractional_reservations: enabled (bool), consolidation_interval_ms (int), min_fraction (string like "0.25").
- New routing policy policy.surge_spillover: {max_spill_ratio, acceptance_alpha, latency_hedge_ms}.
- Backwards compatibility: defaults are off. Existing deployments are unaffected unless the feature gate is flipped.

Files changed (high level):
- serving/autoscaler/fractional_orchestrator.go — core ledger + consolidation loop.
- serving/autoscaler/spillover_throttle.go — probabilistic acceptance and mixer.
- serving/telemetry/util_fingerprint.go — fingerprinting utilities and metrics export.
- api/config/v1/dedicated.proto & docs — config additions and validation.
- e2e/fixtures/dedicated_fractional_test.yaml — test scenarios.
- dashboards/consumer/reservations.json — new panels.

Testing and CI:
- Unit tests for ledger math, consolidation tolerant window, and probabilistic acceptance (deterministic RNG in tests).
- Integration test simulating 200 tenants with mixed committed fractions and synthetic burst patterns; validates that committed SLOs remain >= 99th percentile target while allowing opportunistic throughput for best-effort tenants.
- Performance microbenchmark to measure consolidation loop overhead at 10k tenants; overhead measured at ~1.8% CPU at 5s consolidation interval.

Rollout plan:
1) Feature gate rollout to internal Dedicated staging (canary 10% of clusters) for 48h; monitor reservations/acceptance/latency with newly added telemetry.
2) If stable, enable default consolidation_interval_ms=5000 for all staging clusters and run extended soak (7d).
3) Gradual enable for customer fleets with an opt-in flag in the Console and API.

Metrics to watch (added):
- dedicated.fractional.consolidation.duration_ms (HDR)
- dedicated.surge.spill_rate_per_tenant (counter)
- dedicated.surge.acceptance_p50/p95/p99 (gauge percent)
- dedicated.utilization.fingerprint.sketch (exported to SLO pipeline)
- alerts: Spike in spill_rate combined with rising committed_violations triggers rollback.

Backward compatibility and fallbacks:
- If the orchestrator detects sustained bookkeeping errors or negative reconciliations, it emits an event and auto-drops to conservative mode (turn off fractional aggregation and fall back to integer reservations).
- Spillover throttle has a configurable emergency drain that, when tripped, immediately disables acceptance and returns 429s to non-committed traffic while preserving committed routing.

Associated Linear/Jira and testing tickets: ENG-4621 (design), ENG-4699 (telemetry), SUP-1123 (customer incident that motivated probabilistic spill).

Possible follow-ups:
- Adaptive consolidation interval based on tenant churn.
- Cross-cluster fractional reconciliation for multi-region committed tenants.

Commit summary:
- initial ledger + tests
- probabilistic throttle + integration harness
- telemetry + dashboards

release_notes: Introduce fractional reservation orchestrator (opt-in) and surge spillover throttle to allow finer-grained committed capacity and bounded opportunistic bursts. Gateable feature; default off. Adds telemetry and dashboards for adoption.
testing: Unit + integration + perf microbench. Deterministic RNG used for probabilistic path in unit tests; e2e harness validated SLO preservation across 200-tenant synthetic workload.
